Predictions from a fitted ZISAR model

Source: R/methods.R
predict.zisar.Rd

Fitted or counterfactual means, inflation probabilities and latent field of a ZISAR model.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'zisar'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  type = c("response", "count", "zero", "eta"),
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted "zisar" object.

newdata

Optional data frame of covariates for the same units, in the order of W; needs a model fitted with zisar().

type

"response" for the mean \(E[y_i] = (1 - \pi_i)\mu_i\), "count" for the mean of the negative binomial component \(\mu_i\), "zero" for the probability of a structural zero \(\pi_i\), or "eta" for the latent field \(\eta_i\) (without offset).

...

Not used.

Value

A numeric vector with one value per spatial unit.

Details

Without newdata, predictions are at the fitted values, with the latent field \(\eta\) at its mode given the data.

With newdata, predictions are a counterfactual scenario for the same spatial units: newdata holds one row per unit, in the order of the weights matrix, with some covariates changed. The latent field is recomputed through the spatial multiplier, \(\eta^* = (I - \rho W)^{-1}(X^*\beta + \hat u)\), keeping the predicted random effects \(\hat u = (I - \rho W)\hat\eta - X\beta\) at their estimates, so a change in one unit spills over to its neighbours. An inflation field \(g\) is kept at its mode; with the SAR filter (zero_spatial = "sar") the inflation predictor is recomputed through \((I - \rho_0 W)^{-1}\), so changes in the inflation covariates spill over too. Predictions for new units would need a new weights matrix and are not supported.

Examples

set.seed(1)
sim <- rzisar(10, beta = c(1, 0.5), rho = 0.4, gamma = c(-1, 0.8))
fit <- zisar(y ~ x1 | z1, data = sim$data, W = sim$W)
head(predict(fit, type = "zero"))
#> [1] 0.1924763 0.2642031 0.1660733 0.2783742 0.1892080 0.5107059

# Raise x1 by one in unit 1 only: the change spills over to its neighbours
nd <- sim$data
nd$x1[1] <- nd$x1[1] + 1
delta <- predict(fit, newdata = nd) - predict(fit)
round(head(delta), 3)
#> [1] 2.413 0.087 0.008 0.001 0.000 0.000
